name: Arkansas

agency.name: Arkansas Workers' Compensation Commission (AWCC), Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing

ttd.rateText: 66 2/3% of the individual average weekly wage, rounded to the nearest whole dollar, up to 85% of the state average weekly wage (Ark. Code Ann. § 11-9-501(b)).
ttd.minText: The minimum weekly TD and PPD rate is $20.00 (Ark. Code Ann. § 11-9-501(b), (d)).
ttd.periodLabel: injury or death on and after January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 (state AWW $1,120.68)

waiting.text: Disability benefits are not paid for the first seven days of disability, commencing the day after the injury, if the disability does not last 14 calendar days; if it does, benefits are payable from the day following the injury (Ark. Code Ann. § 11-9-501(a)).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid during the healing period while the employee suffers a total incapacity to earn wages; disability benefits for mental injuries are limited to 26 weeks.

ppd.text: PPD is paid after release to work for permanent impairment; the PPD rate is 75% of the TD rate, rounded, up to $715.00 in 2026 (66 2/3% of AWW up to $154.00 if TD is under $205.35), and amputation or total loss of use of a member is paid at the TD rate (Ark. Code Ann. § 11-9-501(d)). Wage-loss benefits may be added if the impairment affected pre-injury wages.

facts.text: Arkansas has two separate weekly maximums: $953.00 for total disability and $715.00 for permanent partial disability for 2026 injuries.
The weekly minimum of $20.00 has not changed since July 1, 1986, according to AWCC Advisory 2000-1's history table.
Attorney fees must be approved by the Commission; in contested cases half is paid by the employer or carrier and half by the worker out of the award.
Arkansas' no-fault workers' compensation law was created by an initiated act in 1939.
For a compensable injury the work accident must be the major cause (more than 50%) of disability or need for treatment; mental injuries must generally result from a physical injury.

uncertain: Ark. Code text not read directly (published via LexisNexis portal); rules taken from AWCC Advisory 2000-1 (CY2026) and the AWCC Legal Advisor brochure. Any TTD week cap in the Code was not verified; maxWeeks null.
